entities.summary: Marcus Hordeonius Flaccus was a Roman senator who lived during the first century. He was suffect consul for the nundinium of March to April 47 as the colleague of Gaius Calpetanus Rantius Sedatus, and later commander of the Rhine army during the Batavian rebellion. Flaccus was born into a prominent equestrian family in Rome, and his early career was marked by service as a legate in Germania Inferior. He was a key figure in the Roman administration of the province, and his leadership helped to quell the rebellion led by the chieftain Gaius Julius Civilis. Flaccus's experience in the Rhine army also gave him valuable insight into the military tactics and strategies employed by the Roman legions. As a senator, he was known for his eloquence and his advocacy for the rights of the Roman people. Despite his prominent position, Flaccus's life was marked by personal tragedy, including the loss of his son in battle. His legacy as a Roman statesman and military leader has endured for centuries, and he remains an important figure in the history of the Roman Empire.
